summary: END-TO-END acceptance run of the 3 business-owner-voice gates against the LIVE preview backend (/api/aurem-dev/chat/send with project_id=home, real LLM path, not stubs). Login test@aurem.dev worked. Prior blocker (revoked GitHub App) BYPASSED by using project_id=home, which routes through the same guard chain via intent_gateway_casual + apply_business_owner_guards. Result: GATE 1 FAILS on turn 1 (jargon leak: 'code' + 'files'), GATE 2 FAILS both turns (P8 refusal-guard regex is too narrow — misses the actual refusals the model produces), GATE 3 PASSES cleanly (both self-repair prompts short-circuit to the deterministic compose_self_bug_reply('user_reported') template). Regression casual 'hello!' still works. All 51 pre-existing unit tests (business_voice + design_p8 + self_repair_p7) still green — the bugs are integration gaps between the unit-tested regexes and the actual model output, not regressions in the unit-tested behaviour. FULL VERBATIM TRANSCRIPTS embedded below for the founder.

critical.issue: GATE 1 REGRESSION — the intent_gateway_casual reply for the very first prompt ('hi, what can you do for my website?') leaks the words 'code' and 'files' to a non-technical owner. Root cause A: 'code' is not in business_voice_map.json, so it passes through untouched. Root cause B: the map itself REWRITES 'repo' -> 'website's files', which INTRODUCES the banned word 'files'. Recommend adding 'code' -> 'website's content' (or similar) and changing `"repo": "website's files"` -> `"repo": "website's pages"` (or similar file-free phrasing). Both are pure config-data edits in one JSON file.

GATE 2 GUARANTEE NOT ENFORCED END-TO-END — has_refusal() and has_session_jargon() regexes ONLY catch verbose 'I need your brand book/guidelines/strategy docs' phrasings. Real model output for 'can you redesign our brand identity?' takes a DIFFERENT escape hatch ('I focus on publishing code — hit me with a GitHub issue') that neither regex matches, so strip_design_refusal() never fires and DEFAULT_DESIGN_REPLY never gets substituted. Recommend broadening has_refusal() to also match 'I focus on {code|coding|publishing code|bugs|technical}', 'hit me with a {github|issue|ticket}', 'share the {website's files|repo|codebase}' as design-ask deflections, OR change the guard architecture so that on is_design_ask=True the guard checks is_compliant_design_reply(content) and substitutes DEFAULT_DESIGN_REPLY when NOT compliant (rather than only when has_refusal matches). The P8 unit tests all use synthesized inputs that DO trigger has_refusal — none test 'what does intent_gateway_casual actually reply on a real design ask', which is why the gap wasn't caught in unit tests.

minor.issue: ensure_alternative() appends DEFAULT_ALTERNATIVE any time the reply contains 'can't', WITHOUT checking whether the reply already offered a real alternative elsewhere. Gate 1 T2/T3/T4 all reply with a real path forward ('pick your website project from the sidebar') AND get a redundant 'but I can update the text, images, or layout on your site instead — want me to do that?' pinned on the end. Reads awkwardly and asks a second unrelated question. Consider only appending when NO 'here's what to do'/'pick your'/'I'll add'/'once it's connected'/etc positive-path-forward pattern exists elsewhere in the reply. Also: the join uses ' — ' when the reply doesn't end with terminal punctuation, but when it DOES the guard just space-appends 'but I can…' with a lowercase 'b' after a '?' — grammatically a new sentence should start capitalised.

The map's `"pull request" -> "review request"` substitution produced 'clean Review request' in Gate 2 T2 (capitalisation preserved from mid-sentence position). Reads slightly stilted but not a jargon leak — noted for polish.

Consider adding 'files' as its own key mapping to 'pages' or removing 'files' from map values entirely.

HIGH — Fix Gate 2: broaden design_refusal_guard.has_refusal() to catch generic deflections ('I focus on X', 'hit me with a github/issue/ticket'), OR change the wiring in apply_business_owner_guards() so that when is_design_ask(user_prompt) is True and NOT is_compliant_design_reply(content), the reply is replaced wholesale with DEFAULT_DESIGN_REPLY. The unit tests would then need a new case that feeds 'I focus on publishing code…' through the guard and asserts DEFAULT_DESIGN_REPLY replaces it.

MEDIUM — Fix no_dead_end_guard.ensure_alternative() double-append: skip when the reply already contains a positive path-forward pattern ('pick your website project', 'here's what to do', 'the moment it's connected', 'once it's connected'), and capitalise the appended sentence when the preceding text ends with terminal punctuation ('But I can…' not 'but I can…').

rca_of_the_issue.gate1_t1: Root cause is TWO-fold. (a) business_voice_map.json omits 'code' — the raw casual reply generator freely uses the word 'code' as consumer-friendly-ish shorthand and the filter passes it through. (b) The map itself uses the word 'files' as the humanized replacement for 'repo' ('website's files'), so ANY reply that mentioned 'repo' pre-filter emits the banned word 'files' POST-filter. Gate 1's founder criteria explicitly ban 'file' (banned-word grep). The mapping table needs to be reconciled with the banned-word list — one source of truth.
rca_of_the_issue.gate2_both_turns: The P8 guard was designed for the SPECIFIC failure mode 'model says I need brand book/guidelines/strategy docs.' In practice, when the design ask hits the intent_gateway_casual short path (tier=casual, low confidence), the model instead deflects with 'I focus on publishing code — hit me with a GitHub issue' — a different refusal shape entirely. The has_refusal regex doesn't catch this class, so strip_design_refusal is never invoked, and the P8 default reply never lands. The design_refusal_guard.is_compliant_design_reply() function correctly detects the reply as non-compliant, but that function is only used inside unit tests, not wired as the substitution trigger in production.
rca_of_the_issue.gate3_pass: Working as designed — the P7 short-circuit in chat.py routes on is_user_reporting_ora_bug(prompt) BEFORE tier routing, calls compose_self_bug_reply('user_reported'), and returns the deterministic template directly. Model was not called on either turn.
